message:
Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, Structural Dynamicist, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor and Manager, added stiffening cannot do this job within look and weight while added damping can, so the Tuned Mass Damper, defined as Tuned Mass Damper (TMD), stays as pure damping addition. In plain words jacking frequency out of the walking band needs a lot of new steel and weight while two small masses with damping absorb the same resonance. Raising 1.9 Hz to 2.3 Hz needs 46.5 percent more stiffness from the stiffness-increase calculation (E27) called impractical in the retrofit discussion, while added 7.85 kN from the static-weight calculation (E26) is 1.31 percent from the weight-fraction calculation (E72) of 600 kN live load from the live-load estimate (E30), about one person against a crowded deck.

Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, Structural Dynamicist, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor and Manager, the no-weld friction clamp carries both steady weight and crowd dynamics plus a stop hit without fatigue-critical welds, with the stop load fed back into the same bracket. In plain words preload friction does the holding and the bracket must still hold when the mass hits the stops. Slip resistance 32.9 kN per bolt from the slip-resistance calculation (E64) exceeds 13.1 kN combined demand from the combined-load calculation (E65) which already includes 8.40 kN stop hit from the stop-force calculation (E66), about 16 body weights against about 42 body weights of slip capacity per bolt, so margin holds before any bolt-count choice.

Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, I name our joint host-system mounting interface in order from the device ends into the host, viewed between the girders below the soffit at midspan looking along the bridge, as central twin-mass zone to spring-plus-damper zone to single short transverse cross-beam zone to left beam-end-to-girder-web clamp zone and right beam-end-to-girder-web clamp zone to left girder host zone and right girder host zone, with High-Strength Friction-Grip, defined as High-Strength Friction-Grip (HSFG), clamp bolts only in those two beam-to-web clamp zones per the layout sketch (E55) and the transverse clamp sketch (E74), transverse perpendicular to the girders not longitudinal full-span, all below the soffit within girder depth with nothing above deck. In plain words that ordered chain is the only place a clamp callout may land, and I require Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead to jointly confirm that binding and the no-deck-hardware rule before any ready vote, because capacity numbers alone let a leader drift onto the mass frame while listing the correct function.

I am not ready, because my slip and stop numbers stand but the interface binding still needs joint confirmation by Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead.
